title: Pick, confirm and report shortages on a pick-to-light rack
instruction: Pick the order shown by the lamps into the order tote, taking one part for every lit green lamp in front of a bin and nothing from bins whose lamps are dark, and after picking from a bin press its white confirm button; if a lit bin is empty, press its red shortage button instead and take nothing in its place.
context: Unlike 'Kit from the bins whose pick lights are on', which only reads the lamps and picks, this needs the rest of the pick-to-light cycle: pressing each bin's confirm button once its quantity is in the tote (not before), and noticing that a lit bin is empty and reporting it on its shortage button rather than picking a substitute. On real kitting and order-fulfilment lines an unconfirmed pick stalls the order and a silent substitute is a mis-shipped one.
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor; two arms 61 cm apart on a rigid table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm; heights are from the table top. Four dark grey plastic parts bins stand fixed at x = 34, centred at y = 15, 5, -5 and -15: each is 9 x 9 cm inside (11 x 11 cm outside), with 1 cm walls 3 cm tall on a 0.6 cm floor; being 10 cm apart, neighbouring bins share a wall. Each stocked bin holds three identical parts standing in a row along x (at x = 31, 34 and 37), from left to right: yellow plastic cylinders (2.6 cm diameter, 3.5 cm tall, 50 g), grey painted-wood blocks (2.5 x 2.5 x 3.5 cm tall, 60 g), orange plastic cylinders (as the yellow) and blue painted-wood blocks (as the grey). In front of the bins a dark grey plastic lamp strip (2.5 cm along x, 41 cm along y, 1 cm tall) is fixed at x = 27, y = 0. On it, two indicator lamps per bin, plastic cubes of 2.5 cm, centred at x = 27 and at the bin's y + 2 (its left lamp) and y - 2 (its right lamp). Lit lamps are bright green, the others dark. In front of the strip, two push buttons per bin, each a plastic plunger 4 cm along x, 1.4 cm wide and 1.4 cm tall (15 g) lying on the table at x = 23 (its front face at x = 21, its back face 0.75 cm from the strip, which stops it), sliding along x between two fixed dark grey rails (3 x 0.4 x 0.8 cm tall, from x = 22.75 to the strip, 0.1 cm clear either side): a white confirm button at the bin's y + 2 and a red shortage button at its y - 2. A button is pushed in toward the strip and has no return spring. Each trial uses one of three lamp patterns, with three lamps lit over two bins, one of them empty: A, both yellow-bin lamps and the orange bin's left lamp, orange bin empty; B, the grey bin's left lamp and both blue-bin lamps, grey bin empty; C, both grey-bin lamps and the orange bin's left lamp, grey bin empty. The screenshot shows pattern A. A blue plastic order tote is fixed at (11, 0): inside 10 cm along x by 14 cm along y, 1 cm walls 4 cm tall, on a 0.4 cm floor.
scoring: A part is in the tote when its centre is inside the tote's walls and no more than 5 cm above their tops (so a part stacked on another, or still held there, counts); it is placed when it is in the tote, released and at rest with its underside within 1 cm of the tote's floor. A button is pressed once it has moved 4 mm or more from its start (pushed in, or forced out of its rails); a press counts for the rest of the trial, even if the plunger is pulled back. Correct, one point each: every placed part up to its bin's lit lamps; the stocked lit bin's confirm button, if the tote held exactly its lit count from that bin when it was pressed; the empty bin's shortage button. Wrong: every part in the tote beyond its bin's lit lamps (so any substitute for the empty bin, and every part from a dark bin), every part fallen off the table, and every other press (a confirm before or after a short pick, a confirm on the empty or a dark bin, a shortage on the stocked or a dark bin). Score = (correct - 1.5 x wrong) / points available (4 in patterns A and B, 3 in C), not below 0, and at most 0.2 if anything is wrong, so pressing every button scores 0. 1.0 for exactly the parts the lamps show, all placed, the confirm after them and the shortage, and the trial then ends once that has held for 1 s. A part knocked out of its bin onto the table counts neither way. The task's score is the mean over one trial of each pattern. On real arms, count the parts in the tote from a top-down photo of the end state and note each button press, and the tote's count at that moment, from the video.
reset_notes: Stand the picked parts back in their bins, slide every button back out to x = 23 (its front face at x = 21), and set the lamps and empty bin to the next pattern (A, B, C in turn): take the empty bin's three parts out.
fidelity: Approximate. The lamps are fixed coloured blocks, not lights that switch, and stay on after a confirm; the quantity is one lamp per unit, not a digit. The buttons are free plungers sliding in rails with no spring or switch; the scorer records each press. Three fixed lamp patterns, chosen at the start, not by an order system. Parts are plain shapes. Loose objects have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
